agent_notes: The verb הָיְתָה is feminine singular with the masculine name Judah; Ibn Ezra explains it as Judah = the community (feminine), and I follow him. I gloss 'it became', not 'was', because the psalm narrates an event, not a state. 'His sanctuary' is the plain sense of לְקָדְשׁוֹ (קֹדֶשׁ, 'holiness', here a holy place or holy thing); Rashi and Radak read it as the people made holy, Meiri as a share of rank. I keep 'holy place' in the literal layer and leave the question open in the commentary. The tradition about Nachshon appears in Rashi and Radak, but it is midrash, not the psalm's own statement, so I mark it as such.

agent_notes: STEPBible glosses מַה־לְּךָ as 'what? [is] to you'; I corrected it to 'what [is] to you?' as one idiom ('what ails you?'). כִּי תָנוּס is 'that you flee' (imperfect, 'that you keep fleeing'); the sea and Jordan are now addressed in the second person, so the grammar of the psalm changes at verse 5 from report to apostrophe.

The five English versions split: KJV/ASV/Webster put the question into past or present subordinate clauses ('that ye skipped', 'that ye skip'), YLT reads it as an exclamation ('ye skip as rams!'), BBE as 'why were you jumping'. The Hebrew has no question word in this verse: it is the same two cola as verse 4 with the verb in the second person imperfect. I read it as elliptical for 'what [is] to you, that you skip?' carried over from verse 5, which is the reading all commentaries in the packet assume (Metzudat David). The literal layer leaves the verse unsupplemented, with the carried question in brackets.
